summary:
Fort Point is a solid red-brick casemate ring, cut exactly to the footprint map. Its north and west water fronts carry three tiers of arched gun ports with dark backs, and it has a granite base, a parapet, corner towers, a landward sally port, a courtyard of arcaded galleries and a dark lighthouse at the NW corner.
Above it, two International Orange ribs (x 8 and x 22) rise from y 14 to y 29 between pairs of fluted, step-topped cream pylons and stay at y 16 or higher over the fort. The red cables dive from y 36 into concrete housings on a cream Art Deco anchorage with recessed panels, and the deck runs on orange braced bents, half-stepping down from y 34 to y 28.
The silhouette reads as this place: the brick fort with its gun-port tiers, the orange arch leaping over it, and the cream pylons and anchorage. Fort Point as a brick casemate ring with three arched gun-port tiers, sally port, parade galleries, stair towers and a blackstone lighthouse. Over it, an orange terracotta arch between sandstone Deco pylons, with a panelled anchorage and a cable dive. An orange-bent approach viaduct descends on the deck table.
Elements.md and the designer sections are appended to the architect's plan. Six trade-cut parts, no rooms.

fort shell: Fort shell built in parts/fort-shell.mjs: solid brick ring with granite base, parapet and parade rail, tiered embrasures on the north and west fronts, loopholes, sally port and parade galleries. make.sh finishes with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks. The render reads as a brick fort.
polish: The north embrasure at x25 z0 is skipped because it falls inside the N stair tower footprint.
The ring is solid under the tower footprints (x24..27 z0..3, x38..41 z2..5, x4..7 z32..35), so part 2 must place the towers with over:true.
mcd check lists 24 orphan brick_stairs (gallery and embrasure arch heads), a cosmetic report. mcd fit was not run, since this module has no rooms.
The gallery at z18 x24..27 overlaps the sally port; the port is carved last and wins.

polish: Tower quoins and tower bricks at y1..6 are refused (the P1 fort ring is solid there, 289 refused writes); the towers show only above the parapet, and the quoins appear only at y7..9. Recorded in plan.md Notes.
The doorways use the stairTower helper's position (centred on the wall), not plan.md's exact cells (x25..26 z3, x39..40 z5, x7 z33..34); a check against the plan has not been done.
I did not open concept.png; the part follows plan.md and the element list, not the concept art's character.
Only the front elevation and iso tiles were checked by eye; no close-ups of the lighthouse top, the lanterns or the sally port were rendered.
Lamp spacing and the light check were run for the whole site box; no per-plot dark-cell report was made for the fort area alone.
The buttress x38..39 z0..1 (y1..8) is already P1 fort wall, so I did not build it again.

Lay the tower quoins and the parapet coping at the fort's ring so the stair towers' corners and the lantern bases sit on real stone rather than on whatever fort-shell leaves at y1..8.

summary:
pylons and anchorage: P3 pylons and anchorage is built in parts/concrete.mjs: S1/S2 Deco pylon pairs with fluting and stepped crowns, cross beams, the solid south anchorage (x 0..30, z 72..112, y 1..14) with recessed panels on its west, east and south faces, cable housings z 72..80, and anchorage deck piers with cap beams.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt with 0 refused and 0 off-palette writes for this part. fit is OK; check reports only the expected plot-1 floating against y 0.
Plan Notes records the anchorage top-course deviation and the P4 refusals at the housings.
polish: P4 deck: the housings at z 72..75 occupy x 7..9 and 21..23 up to y 35, so the deck's curb, rail and truss cells there are refused by design. The deck part must skip them.

P5 arch and cables: the cable at z 71 (x 8 and 22, y 35..36) lies outside the housing collar's skip band, so P5 must place it. Its cableDive fill at the housing rows will be refused because those cells are already filled by the housing (the same red_concrete).
Plot 1 pylons and anchorage start at y 1 with no y 0 ground, so check reports them as floating against y 0. The plan's hidden footings cover this on placement, so it is not a defect.
No checkboxes exist in plan.md or elements.md, so nothing was ticked. Elements 12 to 16 (pylons, cross beams, anchorage, cable housings, piers) are built; the cable element 21 is P5's.

waste.what: Worked out the anchorage top-course rule by hand: the plan's bottom slabs at y 14 put blocks on a slab, so fit flagged 88 issues and I had to find which cells stand under housings and piers and swap those to full blocks.
waste.cost: one fit run, one edit, one rebuild
waste.tool: A helper for a top course that picks full block or slab from what sits above (anchorageTop), or a plan note saying which cells carry a block.

waste.what: Looked up helper internals (put's carve/over option, cableHousing's collar skip band, whether fill is inclusive) by reading vocab source to avoid refused writes.
waste.tool: Helper docs that state the write guard flag per helper (carve vs over) and the cells each one skips.

waste.what: Imported B from the toolkit by hand after the vocab barrel did not re-export it.
waste.tool: vocab.mjs re-exporting the build library's B and the slab/stairs state helpers.

waste.what: Plot-1 floating check: the structure check counts pylons and the anchorage as floating because plot 1 has no y 0 ground, so every part of this module shows up as floating.
waste.cost: a manual read of the check output to tell expected from real
waste.tool: mcd check --datum or a site option that takes a ground datum, so per-plot kits are not reported as floating.

companions.task: Lay the anchorage as ashlar: the cut-sandstone base and cornice courses, the Deco panel recesses and their inner recesses, and the pylon fluting and stepped crowns, so the course lines and reveals are set by someone who knows bond.
Fit the main cable housings and their collars at z 72..80 and check the cable drop from y 36 to the anchorage top, so the cable meets the housing mouth at the right height.

summary:
deck and truss: parts/deck.mjs builds the plot 1 deck from z 11 to 190 on the DECK_STEPS descent (deckSection per row, with a hand-laid inner row at z 72..75 where the cable housings take the curb, rail and truss), the stiffening truss at x 8 and 22 (z 14..190), 11 Deco lamp posts, and 7 centre hanging lanterns at x 15. make.sh passes with 6558 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; the bridge reads as an orange-railed road with lane lines in the front-right render.</summary>

polish: Road-level light: after my 7 centre lanterns, 28 dark cells remain at y 35 (mostly x 13..17 at the north end z 11..13 and around z 67..78); the approach/arch part's hanging lanterns (P6) cover z 16..62 and 112..190, so re-measure after the merge.

Pier and housing collar cells at x 7..9 and 21..23 are part 3's, not checked here.

companions.task: Hand over the road-level dark-cell list (x 13..17 at z 11..13 and z 67..78 still dim or dark) and ask for lantern spots that clear it with the fewest fixtures, plus the hanging-lantern rows for P6 so the two lists don't double up.
Check the truss joints where the deck steps down at z 124, 137, 150, 164, 177 and 190, and the chord splice where the arch springs at z 14 and 63, before the arch part lands at y 30.

summary:
arch and cables: P5 arch and cables built in parts/arch.mjs: skewbacks at z 11..14 and 63..66, ribs from the intrados table (crown at y 29 for z 33..44), spandrel posts, struts with a lantern each at x 15, and the cable dive from z 71 with no carve.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; the arch part shows 1172 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Nothing is placed below y 16 at x 11..30, z 17..53, and the arch reads as an orange arch in the render sheet.
polish: Floating: the arch's skewbacks rest on land that the kit does not model, and the cable's exposed run at x 8/22 hangs until P3 (housings) and P4 (deck) are merged. The orphans are the fort's, not mine.
Not verified in the merged build: the rib-to-truss merge at z 33..50, and the arch's sightline against the deck truss. Both depend on P3 and P4 being built.

waste.what: Typed the 32-row intrados table and the spandrel/strut heights by hand (rib top = intrados+2, post from top+1 to 29, strut at top, lantern at top+1) for every spandrel z, and checked each for truss/deck clashes by reasoning.

waste.tool: A plan-derived table: rib top, post range, strut and lantern rows per spandrel z, generated from the intrados table, or a spandrelPost option that skips when y0 > y1.

waste.what: Wrote a local put() that checks g.isAir before each set so a rib meeting the deck truss or cable housing merges silently instead of being refused. archRib and spandrelPost already skip occupied cells, but only the helper's own check, which the merge rule relies on and nothing states.
waste.cost: One local helper and one pass through the cable dive.
waste.tool: A documented merge mode in the build library (write-into-air-or-skip-with-report) so parts that meet earlier parts' cells do not each need their own air check.

waste.what: Verified the arch's clearance and the rib/deck merge by reading the render sheet, not by a numeric check.
waste.cost: One render and one Read of the sheet.
waste.tool: A clearance check in mcd check, e.g. --keep-clear box, to flag any cell of a part below a given y inside a box.

companions.task: Lay the skewbacks and the cable housings' smooth_sandstone wedges and their cut_sandstone collars, so the springing and the anchorage meet the arch without my hand-placing the solid blocks.
Light the arch's underside and the strut lanterns. The strut lanterns are placed; the rib-level light depends on the deck lamps and the hanging lanterns that the approach part owns.
Check where the rib meets the deck truss at z 33..44 and z 45..50, where the rib top reaches y 30 and merges into the chord, so the merge is designed, not left to the air-skip.
